text:
Oliver: quick heads-up, I ran a short "light-touch" perfetto run against the rtx-pool serving stack (30s window) to validate a low-overhead probe idea. results below.
Maya: nice — did you sample or full trace?
Oliver: sampling. we record perfetto slices + periodic kernel timeline snapshots every 50ms, plus a light callgraph sample at 2Hz. goal: catch kernel switches & kv-cache churn without pausing requests.
Sasha: curious what overhead you measured. last full nsys we did spiked p50 by ~25% which was unacceptable.
Oliver: end-to-end P50 increased by ~4% for the 30s window on a 16-token workload; tail unaffected. CPU host cpu use up ~6%. GPU utilization telemetry unchanged. so pretty low.
Maya: that sounds promising. any surprises in the timeline?
Oliver: yes — two hotspots.
Oliver: 1) small memcpy bursts from KV cache eviction path that align with an occasional large attention kernel selection. looks like a pathologically aligned batch + eviction -> memcpy -> kernel switch.
Oliver: 2) an extra cudnn fallback kernel for sequence lengths ~512 triggered on 1-2 requests in the window. small but explains one ~12ms blip.
Sasha: so sampling captured both. good. how reliable is 50ms interval? miss anything short-lived (<10ms)?
Oliver: short kernels under 10ms can be missed if they don't coincide with a sample point. that's expected. but the goal is to find recurring patterns or regressions, not 1-off noise.
TJ: question: when you say sampling, did you trigger any additional nvtx markers or hook into runtime? those can add overhead.
Oliver: only lightweight NVTX begin/end on batch boundaries. we avoid instrumenting inner kernels. NVTX adds ~100-200us per boundary in our test.
Maya: can you paste the config you used? want to reuse for dedicated infra.
Oliver: pasted below.
Oliver: ```json
{"trace_type":"light-touch","window_s":30,"kernel_snap_ms":50,"callstack_hz":2,"nvtx_markers":true,"store":"ephemeral"}
```
Sasha: store ephemeral is important — don't want IO to S3 messing with latency.
Oliver: yep. we also rate-limited traces to 1/200 requests and only for requests that hit the max kv cache size (heuristic). that reduced noise and focused on problematic paths.
TJ: nice. what guardrails would you recommend before rolling this in prod as a runbook?
Maya: my proposal: (short list)
Maya: - limit window to <=30s
Maya: - sample <=1/100 requests by default
Maya: - only enable NVTX markers at route-level, not per-kernel
Maya: - write traces to ephemeral SSD and auto-delete after 24h
Maya: - automatic kill-switch if p50 delta > 10% during a trace
Sasha: add: don't enable callstack sampling on Dedicated customers by default (config flag off)
Oliver: agreed. also add a cheap fuzzy-dedupe to avoid repeated traces for the same request fingerprint within 5m.
tracebot: [info] trace queued on rtx-pool-42, id=trace-2026-04-02T18:34:28
Oliver: follow-up: we should add a small post-processor that extracts kernel selection flips and KV hit/evict events and outputs a concise summary. I can prototype a 1-page CSV extractor.
Maya: can you include a column for potential root-cause: eviction/seq-length/kernel-fallback? that will help triage.
Oliver: will do. plan: prototype -> run 100 sampled traces across traffic classes -> see how often memcpy+switch pattern appears. target by EOD Friday.
Sasha: if we see >2% frequency of the memcpy+switch pattern in steady-state, we should add a micro-guardrail: delay eviction by 8ms when a large batch is scheduled.
TJ: flagging: any change touching eviction timing needs perf review and can impact memory pressure. keep that in mind.
Oliver: noted. I'll include metrics for memory headroom in the follow-up.
Maya: thanks, this looks like a safe path to get useful traces without burning prod. :thumbsup:
Oliver: thanks all — ping me if you want access to the raw perfetto files for deeper analysis.
